chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother al-Ḥusayn, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who prays behind one whose prayer is not followed, while the Imam recites aloud. He said: Recite for yourself, and if you do not make yourself hear yourself, then there is no harm.

key_terms.بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: with the recitation of the prayer
key_terms.خَلْفَ: behind, in the position of following in prayer
key_terms.لَا يُقْتَدَى: is not followed as a valid prayer leader

ai.seo_question: What should a person do about recitation when praying behind someone who is not valid to follow as an Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about recitation in prayer when praying behind one who is not to be followed as an Imam. Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructs the person to recite for himself, and states that there is no harm if he does not make himself hear his own recitation.
